headline: Usman Khawaja Asserts Team Knowledge Regarding 2018 Ball Tampering
metaDescription: Usman Khawaja claims Australian players and staff were aware of ball tampering incidents during the 2018 cricket tour of South Africa in new memoir.
aiSummaryBullets: Usman Khawaja alleges that the entire Australian cricket team and staff were aware of ball tampering efforts.
The claims relate to the 2018 series held in South Africa, often referred to as Sandpapergate.
These assertions appear in the newly released memoir written by the cricketer.
aiContextParagraph: In 2018, the Australian men's national cricket team faced significant scrutiny during a tour of South Africa following a ball-tampering incident that gained international attention as Sandpapergate. During the third test match in Cape Town, it was discovered that members of the squad were using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball to gain an unfair competitive advantage. The incident resulted in immediate sanctions for several high-profile players and leadership figures involved in the team at the time. Years later, current cricketer Usman Khawaja has released a memoir in which he claims that awareness of these activities was not limited to those directly sanctioned, but rather extended to all staff and players present during the tour. This perspective adds new commentary to a historical event in Australian sports history that continues to be a subject of discussion and analysis within the cricketing community.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained significant search interest as readers engage with new claims regarding a highly controversial historical event in international cricket.

sources.articleTitle: Khawaja claims all players knew about Sandpapergate ball tampering
